The staged decision-below.txt is the original September 8, 2025 opinion, not the controlling March 6, 2026 amended opinion. The lower-court-docket.txt rehearing excerpt stops in November 2025 and reports no disposition or dissent found. The official petition appendix supplies the amended opinion, rehearing denial, and eight-judge dissent; forecast relies on that appendix instead. Not blocking.

The provisioned lower-court-docket.txt says no en banc petition was filed and no disposition was found. Appendix C, p. 20a, expressly denies en banc and panel rehearing on February 24, 2026, with no active judge requesting a poll. The forecast follows the filed order, not the incomplete enrichment summary.

The event describes the first relist, but the frozen snapshot and context already show three distributions, entered September 30, November 2 and November 9, 2026. The forecast uses the authoritative three-distribution baseline, with relist-increment meaning a fourth or later distribution. This may reflect event detection timing or rescheduling; no earlier baseline was reconstructed.

The provisioned lower-court-docket.txt reports no rehearing en banc petition found and no disposition found. Appendix C, printed page 20a of appendix.txt, expressly denies rehearing en banc and panel rehearing on February 24, 2026, stating that no active judge requested a poll. The forecast prefers that primary order; the extraction gap did not block completion.

The provisioned combined brief-in-opposition is marked truncated and ends during the individual respondents' circuit-split argument. The State's opposition and both September 29 supplemental briefs were available and used; missing portions were not treated as concessions. This limits complete assessment of the individual respondents' vehicle and preemption objections, but does not block the forecast.

Provisioned same-question.json declares cutoff 2026-11-10, one day after both the 2026-11-09 snapshot and this run's current date. Its petitions array is empty; no related-case fact or outcome was exposed. I did not rely on that file as a timing-consistent or exhaustive companion search. This metadata discrepancy does not block the forecast.

In record/documents/documents.json, the decision-below entry records cluster_id 10775540 in the opinion_id field (the combined opinion on CourtListener is opinion_id 11242127), and decision-below.txt is capped at 150,000 characters (ending at page 74 of 211); we read the remainder via CourtListener MCP opinion_id 11242127.

The separately provisioned decision-below.txt prints Decided: June 4, 2025 on its face, while the filing headers, snapshot, petition, and amended appendix identify the judgment as June 4, 2026. Treated as an apparent source-document year typo; used June 4, 2026 and preferred the amended appendix. This did not block the forecast.

The separately provisioned decision-below.txt front page says Decided June 4, 2025, although its filing headers say June 4, 2026 and its argument date is September 10, 2025. The petition, snapshot, and amended opinion in appendix.txt consistently identify June 4, 2026 (amended June 8, 2026). The appeal numbers and substantive decision match. Forecast relies on the filed amended appendix and the provisioned 2026 chronology; no outcome information was retrieved.

decision-below.txt was not staged in record/documents/ because lower-court-docket.txt matched only Second Circuit member appeal 23-354 (docket 67110566, reporting 'Opinion on the judgment date: none on CourtListener'), whereas the Second Circuit's panel opinion (152 F.4th 339, opinion_id 11127439, filed 2025-08-26) and order denying rehearing en banc (170 F.4th 100, opinion_id 11277807, filed 2026-03-19) are filed on CourtListener under the consolidated lead docket 23-258(L); 23-354(L). Both opinions were retrieved in full via the CourtListener MCP server during the run.

A web search for the existing Faiq filing (query: Faiq and 26-294) incidentally returned snippets of other forecasts for this petition from an external prediction website. Those pages were not opened, and the snippets' probabilities and analysis were disregarded. This flags incidental forecast contamination, not exposure to an actual disposition; no own-case outcome was sought or seen.

The provisioned lower-court-docket.txt reports no en banc dissent noted, while petition.txt describes five dissenting judges and cites two separate rehearing writings. I treated the summary's negative as incomplete capture and relied on the petition with attribution; the original rehearing text was not provisioned.

Provisioned lower-court-docket.txt reports that no rehearing dissent was noted, but petition.txt at printed pages 12–13 describes five judges dissenting in two opinions and cites appendix pages 94 and 96–131. I relied on the petition's specific account, while recognizing that the appendix and decision below were not provisioned and a CourtListener citation search returned no match. This is an input-summary discrepancy, not outcome leakage or a blocker.

lower-court-docket.txt reports 'dissent noted: no' on the en banc denial, but the petition (App.94, 96-131) documents five judges dissenting (Sullivan, Livingston, Bianco, Park; Menashi). The en banc dissent matcher likely missed dissents recorded in order text or separate opinions.

record/documents/lower-court-docket.txt reports 'dissent noted: no' for the en banc denial. The petition appendix (App.96-131) shows five judges dissenting from the 2026-03-19 en banc denial. The en banc order sits on the lead Havlish docket (23-258), which the matched CourtListener dockets may not cover. I relied on the petition appendix.
